correctness.rationale: Reconstructing L(Q3) and independently exhausting its graph automorphisms gives exactly the 48 maps induced from the cube. The face counts (24,204,744,1116,528,32) and flag-orbit counts (73,843,2983,4253,2520,480) match. Strict face-size types distinguish all subfaces of a flag, giving regular quotient cells and the signed deletion differential. An independent collapse order reached a three-dimensional regular residual (49,350,684,383) and checked consecutive signed boundary products. Exact Smith ranks (48,302,382) give Betti numbers (1,0,0,1); the only nonunit factors 2 and 6 of boundary degree three give H2 torsion because the outgoing boundary image is free. A direct presentation of the quotient residual kills all 302 generators, avoiding dependence on the separate Armstrong route. Hurewicz realizes the two torsion generators by maps from two-spheres that extend over cells of degrees 2 and 6. The simply connected three-dimensional complex has surjective pi3 to H3 (equivalently, use the Whitehead exact sequence), so a three-sphere realizes the generator of H3. The wedge of these maps is an integral homology equivalence between simply connected CW complexes and thus a homotopy equivalence.
residual_risks: Independent collapse order need not reproduce the frozen collapse count; it establishes the requisite dimension, integral homology and simple connectivity directly. The reference to a four-dimensional chain complex in VERIFICATION.md means four occupied degrees (0–3), not cells of dimension four.

value.rationale: This is a complete integral classification of a natural symmetry quotient whose previously known rational homology looks like a sphere. It resolves whether torsion remains after taking all octahedral symmetries, identifies two independent degree-two summands including a 3-primary component, and realizes the free class by a sphere splitting off in homotopy.
residual_risks: No classification for the rotational subgroup, other graphs, or all line-graph matching quotients is claimed.
